links.note: Hypothesis test, not a result. Pre-data evidence is the freeze timestamp in this file and the S3 checkpoint pushed by the repository run gate; no local commit precedes the data (see PREREG.md section 4).

question: On 14 prime-order 26-bit curves (cofactor 1), where [h]P = P and clearing the cofactor cannot change which points are in the base, does the prime-projected-abscissa base give the same end-to-end counted S as prime-abscissa at 64 columns? (Negative control for MEAS-20261103-ic-cofactor-clear-v2.)

claims.text: Equivalence: the 95% interval of G_0 = sum S(ic-raw) / sum S(ic-clear) lies inside [0.95, 1.05] at 0 GAE per unpriced native operation, so any gain in the main protocol is not an artefact of the arm plumbing.
claims.if_supported: the V2 gain can be read as a cofactor effect

claims.text: The positive control holds: rho-plain / rho-neg has a 95% lower limit above 1.2.

hypotheses.statement: With h = 1 the projection is the identity, so the two bases coincide up to scan bookkeeping and G_0 is 1.
hypotheses.mechanism: [1]P = P; prime-projected-abscissa and prime-abscissa scan the same abscissae in the same order.

arms.description: matched strong rho: rho.negation, the census reference arm
rho.plain: a known counted-operation effect against rho.negation (negation fold, about sqrt 2); proves the paired detector sees a real counted difference
the census ic arm: ic.pipeline, prime-abscissa:size=64, mitm:negation_folded=1
the cofactor-cleared arm on curves where h = 1 (negative control: it cannot matter here)
A/A: the ic-raw arm run again under its own derived algorithm seeds, to give the noise floor of the paired ratio

positive.expected_detection: rho-plain / rho-neg priced S ratio with a 95% lower limit above 1.2 (negation fold, about sqrt 2)

null_population.description: 14 prime-order 26-bit curves (cofactor 1), same five arms and analysis as the main protocol
null_population.why_n: 14 workload clusters, the same number as the main population
matched_on: number of curves and targets per curve

factors.name: binary
factors.how: one ecbench binary for every arm; hash recorded in every record

factors.name: oracle
factors.how: same method params on both ic arms

factors.name: curves
factors.value: 14 prime_search curves, bits 26, seeds 20261200..20261213 (prime order, h = 1)

factors.name: targets
factors.how: ecbench derives the same target for every arm

factors.name: algorithm_seeds
factors.how: ecbench derives each execution's seed from spec.measurement.seed (20261103); recorded in every record

factors.name: host
factors.how: host.json of the session: shared KVM VM, no readable PMU, graded L1

factors.name: isolation
factors.how: per-record isolation level; counted metrics are independent of it

factors.name: preemption
factors.how: local run, no spot capacity, no checkpoint/resume

factors.name: analyst
factors.how: ecbench compare/band commands listed in analysis_plan, fixed before data

comparisons.reason: distance remaining to the matched rho, reported not decided

randomization.arm_order_reason: ecbench measurement.order = alternate over 4 measured rounds after 1 warm-up round

seed_derivation.note: spec.measurement.seed and workloads.target_seed are both 20261104; ecbench derives every execution algorithm seed from them

instance_sampling.rule: 14 prime_search curves with seeds 20261200..20261213, 8 targets each, fixed in advance

blinding.how: no masking: the analysis is a fixed ecbench command list run on all arms identically and its commands and thresholds are frozen here before data

power.note: no power calculation was run; this is an assumption. The interval is reported whatever its width. The 3x threshold is large relative to the interval width expected from 112 paired units (assumed relative half-width of order 10%). Correction: intersection-union over the three weights, no alpha adjustment.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: not measured on this spec: estimated from the 72-execution smoke run of the same binary on this host (5.9 s wall, 20-bit curve), scaled up; no pilot of this spec was run because it would show counted results

primary.name: end-to-end S gain, unpriced work at 0 GAE
primary.unit: ratio of totals sum S(ic-raw) / sum S(ic-clear)
primary.definition: over matched (workload, round) pairs of the 112 V2 workloads and 4 measured rounds, total S of ic-raw divided by total S of ic-clear; S is total GAE over the session floor, all phases (factor base, oracle set-up, relations, linear algebra, solve)
primary.source: records.jsonl cost.s; ecbench compare --a ic-clear --b ic-raw --weight 0

secondary.name: S gain at 0.1 GAE per unpriced native operation
secondary.definition: as M-gain-w0 with every unpriced native operation priced at 0.1 GAE on both arms

secondary.name: S gain at 1 GAE per unpriced native operation
secondary.definition: as M-gain-w0 at 1 GAE per unpriced native operation

secondary.name: trials per relation ratio (mechanism)
secondary.definition: phases[relations].native.trials / native.relations for ic-raw divided by the same for ic-clear; reported only

secondary.name: distance remaining to matched rho
secondary.unit: ratio of totals S(ic arm) / S(rho-neg)
secondary.definition: for ic-raw and ic-clear at each pricing weight; reported, not a gate
secondary.formula: sum S(ic arm) / sum S(rho-neg) over matched pairs

measurement.timed_primary_justification: the primary metric is counted S (group operations), valid at any isolation level; no wall-clock figure is a decision input

stopping_rules.rule: run all 2800 planned executions (112 units x 5 arms x 5 rounds including warm-up)
invalidate and report if any record is not verified, or the A/A, positive or negative control fails

decision_rule.text: valid if the 95% interval of G_0 lies inside [0.95, 1.05] and the positive control (rho-plain / rho-neg) has a lower limit above 1.2. A failure makes the main protocol verdict invalid_controls.
decision_rule.statistic: ratio of totals B/A over matched (workload, round) pairs as defined in src/cryptanalysis/ecbench/compare.rs, workloads as clusters
decision_rule.interval: ecbench compare primary ci95 (linearised delta-method interval, workloads as clusters, Student t); the percentile bootstrap beside it (4000 resamples, seed 20261002) is reported too

literature.claim: the treatment already exists as the prime-projected-abscissa factor base
same lever measured at 1.29x, 1.58x, 3.36x on binary random curves, h = 2, 2, 6; engineering class
fiber-aware oracles recover the same yield from the oracle side; not tested here

inadmissible: any session whose ecbench verify --replay-all reports a problem
any record whose outcome.status is not verified, unless it is a censored pair reported as a bound
any session recorded with git_dirty true, or a binary_sha256 other than the pinned one
any arm result from a session in which the A/A, positive or negative control failed (the verdict is invalid_controls)
